sentences.text: CORAM:

HON'BLE DR. JUSTICE CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA  ORAL JUDGMENT Heard Sri Nagaraja Reddy D., learned counsel for the appellants, who appeared before this Court physically as well as Sri O. Mahesh, learned counsel for respondent No.2, who appeared online.
2. Disputing the validity and the legality of the order that is rendered by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru in M.V.C.No.1691/2018 dated 03.04.2019, the claimants are before this Court by way of this appeal.

The appellant Nos.1 and 2 as parents, appellant Nos.3 to 6 as siblings and appellant Nos.7 and 8 as the grand-parents of the NC: 2024:KHC:32847 deceased Syed Ibrahim moved an application claiming compensation of Rs.45,00,000/- from the respondents on the ground that the deceased Syed Ibrahim (hereinafter referred to as 'deceased' for brevity) died in a road traffic accident occurred in the year 2018.
The Tribunal through the impugned order awarded a sum of Rs.9,98,000/- as compensation.
The appellants are dissatisfied with the sum awarded.
3. Arguing the matter, Sri Nagaraja Reddy D., learned counsel for the appellants contends that the deceased was doing business in buying and selling onions as on the date of accident.
Through the said business, he was earning more than Rs.20,000/- per month.
However, without considering the said fact, the Tribunal, taking notional income of the deceased as Rs.8,500/- per month, awarded meager amount as compensation.
Learned counsel also states that the dependants are eight in number and thus, the amount awarded as compensation has to be increased substantially.

Learned counsel further submits that the accident occurred in the year 2018 and for the relevant period, the Karnataka Legal Services Authority is taking the notional income as Rs.12,500/- per NC:
2024:KHC:32847 month for settling the claims and at least the said figure requires consideration.
4.

Sri O. Mahesh, learned counsel for respondent No.2 contends that as the parents are alive,
appellant Nos.3 to 6 cannot be considered to be dependants of the deceased.
Likewise, the grand-parents i.e., appellant Nos.7 and 8 also were not depending upon the earnings of the deceased as on the date of the accident.

Learned counsel further contends that the notional income adopted by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for settling the claims before Lok-adalath should not be considered for disposal of cases before the Court.
5. Admittedly, the appellants have not produced any substantive proof with regard to occupation and earnings of the deceased as on the date of the accident.
However, an undisputed fact is that the deceased was aged about 20 years at the time of his death.
The said age is the right age to start career and earn profits through the chosen avocation.
The accident admittedly occurred in the year 2018.

Even in case the notional income taken by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority i.e.,
Rs.12,500/- per month for the relevant NC: 2024:KHC:32847 period is considered, the daily wages would come around Rs.417/-.

Therefore, this Court does not find any reason to discard the submission of the learned counsel for the appellants to take the notional income of the deceased as Syed Saleem vs Mohan Reddy K N on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24647432/
3 Rs.12,500/- per month.
6.

sentences.text: Having considered the fact that the deceased died in the capacity of a Bachelor, 50% of the earnings of the deceased are required to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses which he would have incurred for himself had he been alive.
The appropriate multiplier to be applied as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another reported in 2009 SAR (Civ) 592 is '18'.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another reported in 2009 SAR (Civ) 592 is '18'
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Furthermore, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, 40% of the earnings of the deceased is required to be added towards future prospects.

Thus, the total amount which the appellant Nos.1 and 2 are entitled to as compensation will be as under:

Total Compensation Rs. 19,60,000.00  NC: 2024:KHC:32847 8.

Bengaluru through orders in M.V.C.No.1691/2018 dated 03.04.2019 is enhanced from Rs.9,98,000/- to Rs.19,60,000/-.
